Growth is anchored to modern demographic evidence. Movement, departure time and growth transfer are weighted against one archaeological minimum-age constraint. These are conditional expansion estimates, not independently validated dates for humanity’s first arrival.

Source register · Calibration results · Full ensemble

What was actually calibrated?

1,024 seeded draws vary growth, diffusion, departure time and climate resistance. Al Wusta’s 87.6 ± 2.5 ka uranium-series minimum age supplies a one-sided weight; arriving earlier is compatible. The fossil date is not treated as an exact arrival date. Intervals include parameter uncertainty but remain sensitive to the chosen priors.

How does the simulation work?

A least-cost expansion front crosses neighboring land cells at a speed derived from growth and diffusion. Rainfall modifies travel resistance. Fitted results are precomputed; custom scenarios run in a Rust/WebAssembly engine in your browser. In a single draw, local density grows logistically from 1% of capacity after arrival. Density is relative: no ancient population census is claimed.

What does the model leave out?

    Al Wusta is calibration evidence, not an independent test. The other regional estimates have not been validated against held-out archaeological sites. A different origin, climate response, date likelihood or prior can change these ranges.

    Check the prior sensitivity

    Before the Al Wusta constraint, slow-spread draws frequently fail to reach Arabia within the modeled period. The minimum-age constraint filters those draws. This narrows the range under this model; it does not prove its route or departure assumptions.
